concept.name: Pin risk
concept.definition: Pin risk is the uncertainty faced by an option writer when the underlying closes at or very near the short option's strike at expiration: the writer cannot predict whether the option will be exercised, so they cannot determine whether they will wake up after expiration with an unwanted long or short stock position.
concept.intuition: The stock finishes a cent away from your strike on expiration Friday, and you do not know whether you own 1,000 shares on Monday — that unknowable weekend exposure is pin risk.
concept.mechanics: Holders' exercise decisions depend on their own transaction costs, so slightly ITM options may go unexercised and slightly OTM or ATM options are occasionally exercised. Under OCC exercise-by-exception, options $0.01 or more ITM are auto-exercised absent contrary instructions, but exceptions and after-hours news leave the writer guessing. Spread traders face the amplified version: one leg assigned and the other not converts a defined-risk spread into naked stock over the weekend.
concept.failure_modes: The standard failure is the Monday-morning gap: a short spread pinned at the short strike Friday leaves the trader long or short the underlying after partial assignment, and a weekend gap converts a 'defined-risk' trade into a loss far exceeding the spread width.
concept.misconceptions: Closing near the strike does not mean the option 'expires worthless safely' — ATM and even slightly OTM options are sometimes exercised deliberately. Letting defined-risk spreads expire rather than closing them is the classic way pin risk ambushes retail accounts.
concept.example: A trader is short the $50 put; XYZ closes Friday at $49.97. Only some holders exercise, so instead of being flat, the trader is long an unexpected 4,900 shares Monday and must cover a gap at the open.

citations.source: The Options Industry Council (OCC) — Options Exercise FAQ
